target.title: fix(infra): make exec-approvals lock ownership filesystem-safe
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 19, 2026, 6:22 AM (US Eastern Time) / 10:22 UTC.
Last body edit: July 19, 2026, 6:38 AM (US Eastern Time) / 10:38 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 19, 2026, 6:34 AM (US Eastern Time) / 10:34 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

## Summary

This contribution replaces the exec-approvals sidecar lock's inode/device ownership check with nonce-based ownership and applies the same ownership model to the asynchronous update path. It also serializes asynchronous operations per approval file and handles same-process reentrancy without weakening fail-closed authorization behavior.

The change is a clean current-main rebase of the work originally developed in [#111028](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028). Credit and thanks to @Alex-vonAllmen for the original implementation, investigation, and regression coverage.

## What Problem This Solves

The global and host approval policies can be `security=full` and `ask=off`, while an approval-store lock failure still safely falls back to `security=deny`. On virtual filesystems, the asynchronous lock release could fail because ownership was inferred from filesystem identity that is not stable across the descriptor and path views used during release.

As a result, a stale sidecar could make later approval reads fail closed. Changing the policy value cannot bypass a locked or unreadable approval store because the approval store is itself part of the authorization boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lock owner must be identified by a value created with the lock and compared against the current sidecar contents at release time. A random nonce provides that owner boundary across filesystem implementations without relying on inode/device equivalence.

The asynchronous path must use the same lock contract as the synchronous path. A per-path promise queue prevents same-process async writers from racing, while the held-lock map allows a nested same-process read to remain inside the same critical section and observe consistent pre-commit state. Unrelated contention remains fail-closed unless the owner is proven dead or PID-reused.

## User Impact

Approval storage no longer remains stuck solely because a virtual filesystem presents different identity data during asynchronous release. Users with permissive configured policies are no longer exposed to a persistent false `security=deny` caused by this lock-release path, while genuine unreadable or contended authorization state still fails closed.

## Implementation

- Generate a cryptographically random nonce for each exec-approvals lock.
- Persist the nonce in the sidecar payload and require an exact payload match before unlinking.
- Use the same lock implementation for synchronous saves and asynchronous updates.
- Serialize asynchronous operations by approval-file path.
- Track held locks for same-process reentrancy without allowing unrelated reads to bypass a write.
- Preserve stale-owner fail-closed behavior unless the owner is definitely dead or PID-reused.
- Add focused sync, async, ownership, cleanup, and reentrancy tests.
- Keep the release-candidate checklist aligned with the current trusted-tooling validation contract.

## Code-Path Analysis

- Changed surface: `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`, `src/infra/exec-approvals-sync-lock.test.ts`, and `scripts/release-candidate-checklist.d.mts`.
- Runtime entry: `loadExecApprovals`, `saveExecApprovals`, and `updateExecApprovals` resolve the approval file and enter the sync or async lock before reading or committing policy state.
- Owner: the exec-approvals module owns the authorization-store lock lifecycle and its fail-closed policy boundary.
- Callers: gateway approval traffic uses `updateExecApprovals`; synchronous CLI/native paths use `saveExecApprovals` and `loadExecApprovals`.
- Callees: filesystem open/write/rename/unlink operations, process-liveness checks, and approval normalization/policy snapshot helpers.
- Sibling implementation: sync and async lock acquisition now share nonce payload construction and release validation rather than using separate ownership contracts.
- Tests: `src/infra/exec-approvals-sync-lock.test.ts` covers cleanup, nonce ownership, async updates, interleaving, and same-process nested reads.

## Mainline Comparison

- Upstream: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main`
- Base commit: `b9c9140034d7c118a3249def12f29e00e69df849`
- Base commit time: July 19, 2026, 3:31 AM (US Eastern Time) / 07:31 UTC.
- The dedicated branch was rebased cleanly onto this upstream HEAD before push.
- Current mainline dependency verification shows `@openclaw/fs-safe` at `0.4.4` in the lockfile. The historical `0.4.1` observation is therefore not treated as a reason to add an unrelated dependency bump to this focused PR.

## Branch and Base Provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@b9c9140034d7c118a3249def12f29e00e69df849`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/exec-approvals-async-lock@3d5944d5d32c03bd2978795628cd4fa6496249b4`
- The fork default branch was not used for development and was not modified by this work.
- This branch contains only the six original #111028 commits, replayed onto current upstream main with the original author preserved.

## Dependency and Contract Verification

Current mainline already resolves `@openclaw/fs-safe` to `0.4.4`; this PR does not change dependency versions. The correction is at the OpenClaw owner boundary that invokes and releases the approval lock, covering both synchronous and asynchronous paths. The fail-closed behavior remains part of the contract for malformed, unreadable, or genuinely contended authorization state.

## Validation

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- The branch was rebased cleanly onto upstream `main` at `b9c9140034d7c118a3249def12f29e00e69df849`.
- Focused lock regression tests are included in the same change.
- Full build and test execution is intentionally delegated to GitHub Actions for this contribution; no local build artifact is used as evidence.

## Evidence Source Map

- Original real-behavior evidence and sanitized runtime observation: [#111028 evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028#issuecomment-5015182459).
- Related production-path context: [#106777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106777).
- The original report established that approval-store lock failure was converted to fail-closed `security=deny` despite permissive configured policy; this clean branch carries the lock-owner and async-path correction onto current upstream main.
- Current-head CI checks are the authoritative validation for this clean branch after the PR is opened.

## Sanitized Logs

Observed failure pattern, with host and account details removed:

```text
configured approval policy: security=full, ask=off
approval lock release: sidecar remained present on a virtual filesystem
subsequent approval-store read: fail-closed security=deny
```

Expected behavior after the fix:

```text
configured approval policy: security=full, ask=off
approval lock release: sidecar removed after the owning operation completes
subsequent approval-store read: configured policy is available
```

## Media Evidence

This is a non-UI filesystem/runtime change. Screenshots and video are not applicable; the behavior is demonstrated by sanitized runtime observations and focused lock lifecycle tests.

## Risk

The primary risk is accidentally removing a lock owned by another process or allowing a read to bypass an in-flight policy write. Exact nonce matching, per-path async serialization, held-lock reentrancy, and fail-closed contention handling address those risks. The change is limited to exec-approvals persistence and its release-candidate validation contract.

## Rollback

Revert the six commits on this branch. No configuration migration, data migration, dependency migration, or irreversible operation is introduced.

## Docs Updated

No documentation or changelog change is required for this internal runtime correction. The repository contribution guide reserves changelog updates for maintainers.

## Related Issue and PR

- Related prior contribution: [#111028](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028)
- Related production issue: [#106777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106777)
- Original contributor: @Alex-vonAllmen

## Labels Considered

`bug`, `regression`, and `area:infra` may be appropriate; no labels are being applied by this contributor.

## Not Tested / Limitations

- Full repository build and test matrix has not been run locally.
- Current-head GitHub Actions validation for `3d5944d5d32c03bd2978795628cd4fa6496249b4`: 70 checks completed with 0 failures. The [Real behavior proof job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29683639872/job/88184101163) completed successfully; [actionlint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29683602341/job/88183998217) and [no-tabs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29683602341/job/88183998193) also passed.
- The public evidence link above documents the original reproduced behavior; the clean current-main branch carries the lock lifecycle regression coverage and the current-head checks passed.

## AI-Assisted Contribution

This PR was prepared with AI assistance. The contributor has reviewed the lock ownership model, the fail-closed authorization boundary, the focused tests, the dependency contract, and the rebase onto current upstream main.
